With Stellar Tactics, I wanted to recreate the core gameplay from one of my favourite games, XCOM 2. XCOM is a turn-based tactics game where the player commands a squad of soldiers in a fight against alien invaders. The player must carefully move their soldiers across the battlefield to find and accomplish an objective, eliminating any alien threats as they go. This is the gameplay that I wanted to make in this prototype.
I decided that soldiers needed to perform 3 key actions:
Move across the battlefield Fight enemies Interact with the environment My goal was to have a player command a squad of soldiers with these actions against a computer-controlled enemy squad in a simple level. After launching the game and clicking Play, the player is presented with their squad. Before they can fight, they must move a soldier to the door and click on it using the interact action to open it and access the hallway where 2 enemies wait. The player must defeat the enemies using their attack actions: shoot, melee, and grenade. After opening the final door, the player must defeat a second group of enemies, at which point the level ends and the player can either replay it or return to the menu.
With this scenario fully implemented, I accomplished my goal of recreating the core gameplay of XCOM 2 with this small, focused prototype.

FeedFlo provides sensors that monitor animal feed pipes to keep farmers informed about their barns and ensure any issues are discovered and addressed quickly to keep the animals healthy.
My primay roles at FeedFlo were to create and improve features for the web front-end and create a mobile app equivalent to the web front-end. Since I had no prior experience in web or mobile development, I was required to learn a lot and learn it quickly. I developed a strong understanding of JavaScript and React as I worked independently on, and took ownership of, several features for their web front-end’s alert dashboard including adding date-based paging, URL embedded filters for easy copying, and clickable graph elements. I built my understanding of mobile software development while working to build the foundation for FeedFlo’s mobile app. I also built skills with Git, GitHub, and SQL throughout my time at FeedFlo.
My work experience provided me with transferable skills in both self-directed and team-oriented work styles, as I coordinated with team members to build the apps together and integrate with the existing infrastructure of sensors, servers, and databases. I demonstrated flexibility and grew my appreciation for agile software development when the company’s primary direction shifted, requiring me to reprioritize my workload to overhaul how the database schema handles permissions and users to support a new use case.

Fire Emblem is a fantasy series with turn-based tactics where the details often change between games but the fundamentals remain the same: the player commands their units to move within a grid and fight enemies. After finishing the battle, the player is sent back to the hub where they can make more changes to their units and start another battle.
With this gameplay loop implemented, I successfully recreated the key features of Fire Emblem: Three Houses.

content:
With Stellar Tactics, I wanted to recreate the core gameplay from one of my favourite games, XCOM 2. XCOM is a turn-based tactics game where the player commands a squad of soldiers in a fight against alien invaders. The player must carefully move their soldiers across the battlefield to find and accomplish an objective, eliminating any alien threats as they go. This is the gameplay that I wanted to make in this prototype.
I decided that soldiers needed to perform 3 key actions:
Move across the battlefield Fight enemies Interact with the environment My goal was to have a player command a squad of soldiers with these actions against a computer-controlled enemy squad in a simple level. After launching the game and clicking Play, the player is presented with their squad. Before they can fight, they must move a soldier to the door and click on it using the interact action to open it and access the hallway where 2 enemies wait. The player must defeat the enemies using their attack actions: shoot, melee, and grenade. After opening the final door, the player must defeat a second group of enemies, at which point the level ends and the player can either replay it or return to the menu.
With this scenario fully implemented, I accomplished my goal of recreating the core gameplay of XCOM 2 with this small, focused prototype.

XCOM is a turn-based tactics game where the player commands a squad of soldiers in a fight against alien invaders. The player must carefully move their soldiers across the battlefield to find and accomplish an objective, eliminating any alien threats as they go. This is the gameplay that I wanted to make in this prototype.
I decided that soldiers needed to perform 3 key actions:
Move across the battlefield Fight enemies Interact with the environment My goal was to have a player command a squad of soldiers with these actions against a computer-controlled enemy squad in a simple level. After launching the game and clicking Play, the player is presented with their squad. Before they can fight, they must move a soldier to the door and click on it using the interact action to open it and access the hallway where 2 enemies wait. The player must defeat the enemies using their attack actions: shoot, melee, and grenade. After opening the final door, the player must defeat a second group of enemies, at which point the level ends and the player can either replay it or return to the menu.
With this scenario fully implemented, I accomplished my goal of recreating the core gameplay of XCOM 2 with this small, focused prototype.

I wanted to create a prototype of the key features from the Fire Emblem franchise, particularly focusing on Fire Emblem: Three Houses. Fire Emblem is a fantasy series featuring turn-based tactics. While the details often change between games, the fundamental gameplay remains the same: the player commands their units to move on a grid and engage enemies in battle. The main difference from Three Houses that I wanted to focus on was the third-person exploration in a hub-world and how actions in the hub-world affect the tactics gameplay.
When the player starts the prototype, they are in the hub. There they can purchase items from the merchant and change which items their units have. When they are ready, they can use the campfire to start a battle. The items that the units have equipped determine how they can fight, such as the damage or range of their attacks. After finishing the battle, the player is sent back to the hub where they can make more changes to their units and start another battle.
With this gameplay loop implemented, I successfully recreated the key features of Fire Emblem: Three Houses.

I wanted to create a prototype of the key features from the Fire Emblem franchise, particularly focusing on Fire Emblem: Three Houses. Fire Emblem is a fantasy series featuring turn-based tactics. While the details often change between games, the fundamental gameplay remains the same: the player commands their units to move on a grid and engage enemies in battle. The unique element from Three Houses that I wanted to explore was its third-person hub-world exploration and how actions in the hub impact tactical gameplay.
When the player starts the prototype, they begin in the hub. Here, they can purchase items from a merchant and change which items their units have. When they are ready, they can use the campfire to start a battle. The items that the units have equipped determine how they can fight, such as the damage or range of their attacks. After finishing the battle, the player is sent back to the hub where they can make more changes to their units and start another battle.
With this gameplay loop implemented, I successfully recreated the key features of Fire Emblem: Three Houses.

With Stellar Tactics, I wanted to recreate the core gameplay from one of my favourite games, XCOM 2. XCOM is a turn-based tactics game where the player commands a squad of soldiers in a fight against alien invaders. The player must carefully move their soldiers across the battlefield to find and accomplish an objective, eliminating any alien threats as they go. This is the gameplay that I wanted to make in this prototype.
I decided that soldiers needed to perform 3 key actions:
Move across the battlefield Fight enemies Interact with the environment My goal was to have a player command a squad of soldiers with these actions against a computer-controlled enemy squad in a simple level. After launching the game and clicking Play, the player is presented with their squad. Before they can fight, they must move a soldier to the door and click on it using the interact action to open it and access the hallway where 2 enemies wait. The player must defeat the enemies using their attack actions: shoot, melee, and grenade. After opening the final door, the player must defeat a second group of enemies, at which point the level ends and the player can either replay it or return to the menu.
With this scenario fully implemented, I accomplished my goal of recreating the core gameplay of XCOM 2 with this small, focused prototype.

FeedFlo provides sensors that monitor animal feed pipes to keep farmers informed about their barns and ensure any issues are discovered and addressed quickly to keep the animals healthy.
My primay roles at FeedFlo were to create and improve features for the web front-end and create a mobile app equivalent to the web front-end. Since I had no prior experience in web or mobile development, I was required to learn a lot and learn it quickly. I developed a strong understanding of JavaScript and React as I worked independently on, and took ownership of, several features for their web front-end’s alert dashboard including adding date-based paging, URL embedded filters for easy copying, and clickable graph elements. I built my understanding of mobile software development while working to build the foundation for FeedFlo’s mobile app. I also built skills with Git, GitHub, and SQL throughout my time at FeedFlo.
My work experience provided me with transferable skills in both self-directed and team-oriented work styles, as I coordinated with team members to build the apps together and integrate with the existing infrastructure of sensors, servers, and databases. I demonstrated flexibility and grew my appreciation for agile software development when the company’s primary direction shifted, requiring me to reprioritize my workload to overhaul how the database schema handles permissions and users to support a new use case.

I wanted to create a prototype of the key features from the Fire Emblem franchise, particularly focusing on Fire Emblem: Three Houses. Fire Emblem is a fantasy series featuring turn-based tactics. While the details often change between games, the fundamental gameplay remains the same: the player commands their units to move on a grid and engage enemies in battle. The unique element from Three Houses that I wanted to explore was its third-person hub-world exploration and how actions in the hub impact tactical gameplay.
When the player starts the prototype, they begin in the hub. Here, they can purchase items from a merchant and manage their units’ inventories. When they are ready, they can use the campfire to start a battle. The equipped items determine how each unit can fight, such as the damage or range of their attacks. After completing the battle, the player returns to the hub where they can make more changes to their units and start another battle.
With this gameplay loop implemented, I successfully recreated the key features of Fire Emblem: Three Houses in my prototype Emergence.

With Stellar Tactics, I wanted to recreate the core gameplay from one of my favourite games, XCOM 2. XCOM is a turn-based tactics game where the player commands a squad of soldiers in a fight against alien invaders. The player must carefully move their soldiers across the battlefield to find and accomplish an objective, eliminating any alien threats as they go. This is the gameplay that I wanted to make in this prototype.
I decided that soldiers needed to perform 3 key actions:
Move across the battlefield Fight enemies Interact with the environment My goal was to have a player command a squad of soldiers with these actions against a computer-controlled enemy squad in a simple level. After launching the game and clicking Play, the player is presented with their squad. Before they can fight, they must move a soldier to the door and click on it using the interact action to open it and access the hallway where 2 enemies wait. The player must defeat the enemies using their attack actions: shoot, melee, and grenade. After opening the final door, the player must defeat a second group of enemies, at which point the level ends and the player can either replay it or return to the menu.
With this scenario fully implemented, I accomplished my goal of recreating the core gameplay of XCOM 2 with this small, focused prototype.
